documents.title: Configure VPN Client on your Computer, Tablet, or Phone
documents.content:
Overview

Download and configure the UCSD Virtual Private Network (VPN) Cisco Secure Client on your
computer, phone, or tablet. If you would like more information about the campus VPN, see the
Virtual Private Networks (VPN) at UCSD page.

See the steps for your operating system:

Windows 11 / 10
Mac OS X
Android / Chromebook
iPhone / iPad
GNU / Linux

Critical Concepts

The VPN only needs to be installed if you need access to Trusted Resources.
You will need your Active Directory (AD) username and password. If you don't remember

your AD username or password, you can either reset it at password.ucsd.edu or contact your
department's systems administrator.

Your AD username is usually the first part of your UCSD email address (before

@ucsd.edu).

If you are required to comply with the Secure Connect mandate, you will be required to

have Trellix (aka FireEye) Endpoint Security (HX) and Qualys Cloud Agent installed on your

device. If you do not already have these software installed, you will be redirected to the

installation instructions during the VPN installation process. For more information about

Trellix and Qualys, please visit Required Software.

Two-Step Login

Two-step login is required for everyone when connecting to the VPN. Information for
registering for Duo Two-Step can be found on the Register for Two-Step Login (Duo) article.

Those required to comply with Secure Connect NAC must select a secure-connect
group.

Using a passcode or an alternative method to perform two-step login requires a little bit of
extra typing to get it to work as expected. If you are using two-step login on the VPN for the
first time, we highly recommend reviewing the instructions on Duo Two-Step on VPN
knowledge article.

Steps to take

Windows 11 / 10

Before you begin: You must log into your computer with administrator rights.

1. Download the corresponding Cisco Secure Client for your Windows version. This will be
the file with the name that ends in "core-vpn-predeploy-k9". then click Run.

NOTE: If you encounter any issues accessing this Sharepoint link, please try
logging into mcvpn.ucsd.edu to access the download link titled Windows Client
Download.

If you are unsure if your device is a Windows-on-Arm device, navigate to your
system's Settings > System > About. Under "Device Specifications" > "System type",
it will say "ARM-based processor" if your device is a Windows-on-Arm device.
2. Install the Cisco Secure Client:
a. Click Next to begin the installation.
b. Accept the terms, and click Next.
c. Click Install.
d. You may be asked if you want to allow the following program to install software on
this computer - Click Yes.
e. Click Finish.
3. If you are not a paid employee or are not being enforced as part of the Secure Connect
project on the VPN, skip to step 6.
a. If you are unsure if you are being enforced, see Secure Connect Timelines and
Updates for the Secure Connect VPN rollout timeline.
4. Download the VPN Cisco Secure Client - ISE Posture module. This will be the file name
that ends in "iseposture-predeploy-k9".
5. Install the Cisco Secure Client - ISE Posture Module:
a. Click Next to begin the installation.
b. Accept the terms, and click Next.
c. Click Install.

d. You may be asked if you want to allow the following program to install software on

this computer - Click Yes.

e. Click Finish.

6. Run the Cisco Secure Client.

Click on the Windows Start Button (this will display the Windows Start Menu).

Click on All Apps and choose the Cisco folder.

7. In the first window, enter vpn.ucsd.edu in the box and click on the Connect button to the

right.

8. A second window will appear. Select your desired connection profile from the Group drop-down menu:

2-Step Secured options:
split - Route only campus traffic through the UCSD VPN. All other traffic goes

through your normal Internet provider.
allthruucsd - Route all traffic through the UCSD VPN.
Use this option when accessing the CMS.

secure-connect options - Needs to be used if you are required to comply with
Secure Connect NAC.

split - Similar to "2-Step Secured - split" but for devices required to comply
with Secure Connect NAC.

allthruucsd - Similar to "2-Step Secured - allthruucsd" but for devices
required to comply with Secure Connect NAC.

9. Enter your Active Directory username and password. For Duo Two-Step, please stop
here and review how to use two-step on the VPN.
10. Click Ok.

11. Next, navigate to "captive-portal.ucsd.edu". If you are required to comply with Secure
Connect enforcement on the VPN, this page will say "UC San Diego VPN Security" at the
top. If you do not see this, or already have the Posturing Agent (ISE Posture Module)
installed, please skip to step 17.
12. On the page that appears, click "Start". Then click on the "This is my first time here"
dropdown menu.
13. Under step 1, click on the "Click here to download and install Agent" link. This will
download the required module to your device.

14. You may get an error when downloading the module. If so, hover the mouse over the
download, click the 3 dots, and click "Keep"

15. When the module finishes downloading, click on the download to initiate the installation of
the module.

1. If you get the error "SmartScreen can't be reached right now", click "Run", then click
"Yes".

16. In the window that appears, click "Connect". Once the installation finishes, click "Quit".
1. You can now close out the "captive-portal.ucsd.edu" website.

17. If the device does not have all of the required software for connecting to the VPN, you will
be redirected to articles on how to become compliant.

1. If you are not already logged into the "Services & Support" website, you will then
need to use your Active Directory (AD) credentials to log in and access the articles.
2. Follow the steps in the articles to download and install the required software.
3. Once your device has all of the required software, the ISE Posture module should
automatically re-scan your device to check again for compliancy.

1. If the module does not automatically re-scan your device, you can click the
"Scan Again" button in the VPN client under "ISE Posture" to re-run the scan.
18. To disconnect from the VPN after your session is finished:
1. Click on the Windows Start Button (this will display the Windows Start Menu). Click
on All Apps and choose the Cisco Secure Client.
2. When the window appears, click on the Disconnect button.

macOS

You must log into your computer with administrator rights.

Computer must be running macOS 14 and above to use the Cisco Secure Client. Older Mac
operating systems are no longer supported.

1. If the client was previously installed on your device, uninstall old client by following these
steps (this will require a computer restart):

a. Go to your Applications folder.
b. Locate and double-click on the Cisco folder.
c. Double-click on Uninstall Cisco Secure Client.
d. Click Uninstall.
e. Enter your computer's administrator password.
f. You will then see a message saying that "Cisco Secure Client has been uninstalled".

Click Close.

g. Restart your computer.

2. Download the VPN Cisco Secure Client.

NOTE: If you encounter any issues accessing this Sharepoint link, please try

logging into mcvpn.ucsd.edu to access the download link titled MAC Client Download.

3. After the download completes, double-click the cisco-secure-client-macos installation

file. The installer icon shown below will appear on your desktop.

4. Run the installation package by double-clicking on the Cisco Secure Client package
image.
5. Install the Cisco Secure Client:

a. Click Continue to begin the installation.
b. Click Continue.
c. When the Software License Agreement window appears, click Agree to accept.
d. Select the module options that you need:

a. If you are enforced as part of the Secure Connect project on the VPN,
deselect all of the options except for "ISE Posture".
b. If you are not a paid employee or are not being enforced as part of the Secure
Connect project on the VPN, deselect all of the options, including "ISE Posture".
c. If you are unsure if you are being enforced, see Secure Connect Timelines and
Updates for the Secure Connect VPN rollout timeline

e. Click Continue.
f. Click Install.
g. If prompted, enter your Administrative (system) username and password.
h. You may get the following "Action Required" pop-up . If you do, click on "Open
System Settings" on the bottom of the pop-up.

i. In the Systems Settings window that appears, toggle "Cisco Secure Client -
AnyConnect VPN Service" on. If prompted, enter your Administrative (system)
username and password.
j. You may then get the following "Action Required" pop-up . If you do, click on "Open
System Settings" on the bottom of the pop-up.

k. In the System Settings window that appears, click Allow.
l. When you see the "Install Succeeded" pop-up window, click Close to continue.
m. You may then get the following pop-up. Click Allow.

6. Run the Cisco Secure Client by going to the Cisco folder in Applications and double-clicking the Cisco Secure Client.
7. Enter vpn.ucsd.edu in the "Connect to" field.
8. Press the return (enter) key.
9. Select your desired connection profile from the Group drop-down menu:

2-Step Secured options:
split - Route only campus traffic through the UCSD VPN. All other traffic goes

through your normal Internet provider.
allthruucsd - Route all traffic through the UCSD VPN.
Use this option when accessing the CMS.

secure-connect options - Needs to be used if you are required to comply with
Secure Connect NAC.

split - Similar to "2-Step Secured - split" but for devices required to comply
with Secure Connect NAC.

allthruucsd - Similar to "2-Step Secured - allthruucsd" but for devices
required to comply with Secure Connect NAC

10. Enter your AD username and password. For Duo Two-Step, please stop here and review
how to use two-step on the VPN.
11. Click OK.

12. Next, navigate to "captive-portal.ucsd.edu". If you are required to comply with Secure
Connect enforcement on the VPN, this page will say "UC San Diego VPN Security" at the
top. If you do not see this, or already have the Posturing Agent (ISE Posture Module)
installed, skip to step 18.
13. On the page that appears, click "Start". Then click on the "This is my first time here"
dropdown menu.
14. Under step 1, click on the "Click here to download and install Agent" link. This will
download the required module to your device

15. When the module finishes downloading, navigate to the Downloads folder and double-click on the file with the ".dmg" extension. Then double-click the "Cisco Network Setup
Assistant" to initiate the installation of the module.
16. In the window that appears, click "Connect". Once the installation finishes, click "Quit".

1. You can now close out the "captive-portal.ucsd.edu" website.
17. If you encounter the following prompt or any similar prompts from "csc_iseposture", click
"Don't Allow".

18. Upon connecting to one of the secure-connect connection profiles, a compliance
module will automatically install on your device. Once this has finished installing, the ISE
Posture module will evaluate your device's compliance to security standards.
19. If the device does not have all of the required software for connecting to the VPN, you will
be redirected to articles on how to become compliant.

1. If you are not already logged into the "Services & Support" website, you will then
need to use your Active Directory (AD) credentials to log in and access the articles.
2. Follow the steps in the articles to download and install the required software.
3. Once your device has all of the required software, the ISE Posture module should
automatically re-scan your device to check again for compliancy.

1. If the module does not automatically re-scan your device, you can click the
"Scan Again" button in the VPN client under "ISE Posture" to re-run the scan.
20. To disconnect from the VPN after your session is finished:
1. Open the Cisco Secure Client application.
2. Click on the Disconnect button.

Android / Chromebook

1. Open the Google Play store on your Android or Chromebook device and search for "Cisco
Secure Client".

1. For Chromebooks, if you do not have the Google Play store, follow these steps to
get the Google Play store app. (Note: you must be signed into a non-guest account on
your Chromebook.)
2. Click Install.

3. Enter the VPN Connection:

a. Open the Cisco Secure Client app.

b. Select Connections.

c. Select Add New VPN Connection.

d. In Description enter: UCSD

e. In Server Address enter: vpn.ucsd.edu

f. Click Done.

4. On the Cisco Secure Client home screen, turn on Cisco Secure Client by selecting the Off
toggle (it will change to On).
5. A second window will appear. Select your desired connection profile from the Group drop-down menu:

2-Step Secured options:
split - Route only campus traffic through the UCSD VPN. All other traffic goes

through your normal Internet provider.
allthruucsd - Route all traffic through the UCSD VPN.
Use this option when accessing the CMS.

6. In the username field, enter your Active Directory (AD) username.
7. In the Passcode field, enter your Active Directory (AD) password. For Duo Two-Step,
please stop here and review how to use two-step on the VPN.
8. Click Connect.
9. To disconnect from the VPN after your session is finished:

a. Open the Cisco Secure Client.
b. On the Cisco Secure Client home screen, turn off Cisco Secure Client by clicking the
On toggle (it will change to Off).

iPhone / iPad

1. Using your iPhone or iPad, download the Cisco Secure Client app from the App Store.

2. Add a VPN Connection:
a. Click on Connections.
b. Click Add VPN Connection.
c. Fill out the requested information:
Description: UCSD VPN
Server Address: vpn.ucsd.edu
d. Click Save.
e. When prompted if you would like to "Add VPN Configurations", click Allow.

3. Connect to the VPN:
On the main page, toggle the Cisco Secure Client VPN button to On position.

Select your desired connection profile from the Group drop-down menu:
a. Only use the ones labeled "2-Step Secured" or "secure-connect".
b. 2-Step Secured options:
split - Route only campus traffic through the UCSD VPN. All other traffic
goes through your normal Internet provider.
allthruucsd - Route all traffic through the UCSD VPN.
Use this option when accessing the CMS.

Enter your Active Directory (AD) credentials.
Click Connect.
A Duo push will be sent to the Duo app; approve it and then return to the Cisco
Secure Client app.
Accept the connection.

4. To disconnect from the VPN after your session is finished, toggle the Cisco Secure Client
VPN button to the OFF position.

Linux

Before you begin: You must either log into your computer with administrator rights or have the
system root password.

Debian/Ubuntu/Linux Mint:

1. Download the VPN Cisco Secure Client.

1. If you have a x64-based system, choose the file named cisco-secure-client-linux64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-deb-k9.tgz (the version may be different).

2. If you have an ARM64-based system, choose the file named cisco-secure-client-linux-arm64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-deb-k9.tgz (the version may be different).

2. Open your terminal application. Navigate to the Downloads folder by typing in cd

Downloads.

3. To decompress the archive, follow the instructions below for your respective system, then

press enter.

1. For x64-based systems: type tar -xzf cisco-secure-client-linux64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-deb-k9.tgz (you may need to modify the filename if the version has

changed).

2. For ARM64-based systems: type tar -xzf cisco-secure-client-linux-arm64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-deb-k9.tgz (you may need to modify the filename if the version

has changed).

4. To install the VPN package, follow the instructions below for your respective system, then

press enter. You may need to enter your password.

1. For x64-based systems: type sudo dpkg -i cisco-secure-client-vpn_5.1.16.194_amd64.deb (you may need to modify the filename if the version has

changed).

2. For ARM64-based systems: type sudo dpkg -i cisco-secure-client-vpn_5.1.16.194_arm64.deb (you may need to modify the filename if the version has

changed).

5. If you are not a paid employee or are not being enforced as part of the Secure Connect

project on the VPN, skip to the "To use" section.

a. If you are unsure if you are being enforced, see Secure Connect Timelines and

Updates for the Secure Connect VPN rollout timeline.

6. To install the ISE posture module, follow the instructions below for your respective system,

then press enter. You may need to enter your password.

1. For x64-based systems: type sudo dpkg -i cisco-secure-client-iseposture_5.1.16.194_amd64.deb (you may need to modify the filename if the

version has changed).

2. ARM64-based systems: the ISE posture module is not currently supported on these

systems.

Other (e.g. Arch):

1. Download the VPN Cisco Secure Client.
1. If you have a x64-based system, choose the file named cisco-secure-client-linux64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-rpm-k9.tgz (the version may be different).
2. If you have an ARM64-based system, choose the file named cisco-secure-client-linux-arm64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-rpm-k9.tgz (the version may be different).

2. Open your terminal application. Navigate to the Downloads folder by typing in cd
Downloads.
3. To decompress the archive, follow the instructions below for your respective system, then
press enter.

1. For x64-based systems: type tar -xzf cisco-secure-client-linux64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-rpm-k9.tgz (you may need to modify the filename if the version has

changed).

2. For ARM64-based systems: type tar -xzf cisco-secure-client-linux-arm64-5.1.16.194-predeploy-rpm-k9.tgz (you may need to modify the filename if the version

has changed).

4. To install the VPN package, follow the instructions below for your respective system, then

press enter. You may need to enter your password.

1. For x64-based systems: type sudo rpm -ivh cisco-secure-client-vpn-5.1.16.194-1.x86_64.rpm (you may need to modify the filename if the version has changed).

2. For ARM64-based systems: type sudo rpm -ivh cisco-secure-client-vpn-5.1.16.194-1.aarch64.rpm (you may need to modify the filename if the version has

changed).

5. If you are not a paid employee or are not being enforced as part of the Secure Connect

project on the VPN, skip to the "To use" section.

a. If you are unsure if you are being enforced, see Secure Connect Timelines and

Updates for the Secure Connect VPN rollout timeline.

6. To install the ISE posture module, follow the instructions below for your respective system,

then press enter. You may need to enter your password.

1. For x64-based systems: type sudo rpm -ivh cisco-secure-client-iseposture-5.1.16.194-1.x86_64.rpm (you may need to modify the filename if the version has

changed).

2. ARM64-based systems: the ISE posture module is not currently supported on these

systems.

To use:

1. Run the Cisco Secure Client by searching for the application called Cisco Secure Client.
2. Enter vpn.ucsd.edu in the Connect to field.
3. Click Connect.
4. Select your desired connection profile from the Group drop-down menu:

2-Step Secured options:
split - Route only campus traffic through the UCSD VPN. All other traffic goes

through your normal Internet provider.
allthruucsd - Route all traffic through the UCSD VPN.
Use this option when accessing the CMS.
secure-connect options - Needs to be used if you are required to comply

with Secure Connect NAC.
split - Similar to "2-Step Secured - split" but for devices required to

comply with Secure Connect NAC.
allthruucsd - Similar to "2-Step Secured - allthruucsd" but for devices

required to comply with Secure Connect NAC

5. Enter your AD username and password. For Duo Two-Step, please stop here and
review how to use two-step on the VPN.
6. Click Connect. If you are not required to comply with the Secure Connect NAC VPN or
your VPN already shows "ISE Posture", skip to step 12.

7. You will be redirected to a page with "UC San Diego VPN Security" at the top. On this
page, click "Start".
8. If you do not have the required module for your VPN instance, click on the "This is my first
time here" dropdown menu.
9. Under step 1, click on the "Click here to download and install Agent" link. This will
download the required module to your device.
10. When the module finishes downloading, click on the download to initiate the installation of
the module.
11. In the window that appears, click "Connect". Once the installation finishes, click "Quit".
12. To disconnect from the VPN after your session is finished:

a. Open the Cisco Secure Client application.
b. Click on the Disconnect button.
